Base recipe from Mrs Kang at Seoul Mart in Chinatown, tweaked every batch. Napa cabbage, brine soak, paste, jar. Log below.

Base per 3 kg napa: 10% brine (300 g coarse sea salt in 3 L water), 6 h soak, rinse 3 times. Paste: 90 g gochugaru (coarse flakes, Taekyung brand), 40 g garlic, 20 g ginger, 1 nashi pear grated, 60 ml anchovy sauce (aekjeot), 30 g salted shrimp (saeujeot), glutinous rice porridge (2 tbsp rice flour in 200 ml water), 6 spring onions, 1 daikon in matchsticks (250 g).

## 2024-10-05, K1

- 3.2 kg napa (2 heads, £4.60 at Seoul Mart)
- soak 6 h, turned at 3 h
- paste as base
- 2 days at 19°C, then fridge
- verdict: good but too salty. Rinse more.

## 2024-11-16, K2

- 3.0 kg napa, rinsed 4 times
- gochugaru up to 110 g for the truck crowd
- 1 day at 20°C, fridge
- verdict: better. Tash: "needs more heat". Tash always says that.
- used most of it in kimchi fried rice for the [[Weeknight stir fry]] slot on Thursdays

## 2025-01-11, K3

- 6.1 kg napa, double batch, 4 heads
- soak 5 h only (colder kitchen, 14°C, so it went slower anyway)
- added 15 g sugar, Mrs Kang said the pear wasn't sweet enough in winter
- packed in two 3 L Kilners, weights on top ([[Fermentation weights and airlocks]])
- 3 days at 14°C, fridge
- verdict: best one. Menu code KC-11, kimchi cheese toastie, £7.

## 2025-03-02, K4

- 3.1 kg napa
- vegan test: anchovy sauce and shrimp swapped for 2 tbsp soy + 1 tbsp white miso + 10 g kombu soaked
- 2 days at 18°C
- verdict: 80% there. Lacks the funk. Keep the vegan version as a side option, code KC-11V.

## Rules so far

- 10% brine, 5 to 6 h, rinse 3 or 4 times. Taste a rib after rinsing: should be like a crisp, not like seawater.
- 1 to 3 days out depending on room temp, then fridge.
- way faster and wetter than the dry-salted kraut, see [[Sauerkraut]] for the comparison.
- fizzes when you open it at day 2. That's right.
